title: Clear and swallow the lock-screen wake key so it is not typed as a password character
head: d64d6f25c6fb
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The open password-visibility PR #13183 needs a combined key handler, not an either-side conflict resolution
leads.consequence: The two unstacked PRs edit the same handler and the three-way merge has conflict markers. If a resolution keeps this PR's unconditional `event.accepted = clearPassword` but loses #13183's Copy/Cut check, a revealed password (TextInput.Normal in #13183) can be selected and copied into the system clipboard on an awake lock screen. If it keeps #13183's handler alone, the wake-key swallow from this PR is lost. A combined resolution must handle blank/wake, Escape/Ctrl+U, and Copy/Cut independently. This is a conditional integration hazard, not a claim either submitted head currently leaks a password.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N3 (#13183 conflict); copy-guard loss depends on a hypothetical bad merge resolution

leads.summary: Held wake keys can still be typed by auto-repeat after the first keypress is swallowed
leads.consequence: For a nonvideo wallpaper the monitor poll is off; first keypress while blank calls runWake, clearing displaysBlank immediately, and is accepted. A repeat press of the still-held key is therefore not accepted by the handler and TextInput inserts it, potentially many times during a slow display wake. Open, unstacked #7806 addresses the same held-key repeat in a conflicting hunk, and its description reports on-device reproduction, but no live compositor/display is assigned here. Explicitly account for repeated wake keys when integrating.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Q1 mechanism (only first key swallowed); published as Details note with source qualifier; #7806 same-block conflict verified from diff

leads.summary: Input-method commit events bypass Keys.onPressed and could still type into a blank password field
leads.consequence: Qt routes QInputMethodEvent through the item's inputMethodEvent, not Keys.onPressed; TextInput inserts its commitString. An IME or virtual keyboard commit delivered while displaysBlank remains true therefore inserts its text and then onTextChanged requests wake, without invoking the new clear/accept path. Whether the compositor actually delivers such a commit while DPMS-blanked needs an isolated IME/Wayland run; no live lock session is available.
leads.triage: IME hypothesis, pre-existing, also in Opus Q1; dropped

leads.summary: The keypad recovery PR #12667 conflicts in the same key handler and needs a wake-aware resolution
leads.consequence: Unstacked #12667 maps NumLock-desynced cursor/keypad keys to digits in `insertKeypadDigit` after wakeRequested. Its key handler conflicts with this PR's `clearPassword` assignment. Keeping only one side drops the other's feature, while calling `insertKeypadDigit(event)` before checking the blank state inserts the swallowed wake keypad digit. First branch on the snapshotted blank flag, then apply the keypad mapping on nonblank input. #12667's model-only test will not catch a bad conflict resolution in the handler.

leads.summary: New source-regex test passes when password clearing is disabled
leads.consequence: A plausible regression, changing `if (clearPassword) root.passwordTextEdited("")` to `if (false && clearPassword) root.passwordTextEdited("")`, leaves the wake key accepted but leaves a half-entered password intact. All four test assertions still pass because they look for fragments, not the conditional clear's behavior or the surrounding expression. Add a Qt/Quickshell input fixture (or an equivalent handler simulation) that starts with a nonempty password and checks both the swallowed first press and cleared field; keep a nonblank key as a control. The asserted Keys.BeforeItem property is already Qt's default, so that assertion alone establishes no behavior change.

leads.summary: Open #9211 duplicates the wake-key handler and its source-shape test conflicts with this PR
leads.consequence: Independent #9211 also checks displaysBlank then accepts the wake key. Its three-way merge with this PR conflicts in Keys.onPressed. Choosing this PR's handler and retaining #9211's resume timer causes #9211's regex assertion for `var wasBlank ... if (wasBlank)` to fail; choosing #9211 alone drops this PR's explicit password clear. Coordinate/deduplicate both PRs, preserving any desired resume timer and retesting the combined behavior instead of stacking incompatible source-shape assertions.
leads.triage: #9211 duplicate wake-key swallow in same block: verified by coordinator (gh pr diff 9211) and Opus self-check (merge-tree conflict)

leads.summary: DPMS status is a logical request, not a physical screen-visible acknowledgement
leads.consequence: When video wallpaper polling is active, `screenBlank` replaces displaysBlank with `!monitorDpms[name]`. Hyprland v0.51.1 switches `m_dpmsStatus = on` before enabling/presenting the output, so a key arriving after the status flips but before a panel has lit can be treated as normal password input while the user still sees a dark display. Conversely a fast key following this PR's wake also sees displaysBlank=false before the child has enabled the screen. The duration and actual delivery are hardware dependent; settle with a timed multi-monitor/slow-panel integration test if this distinction matters to the promise that dark-screen input is swallowed.
leads.triage: Hyprland DPMS timing hypothesis (video wallpaper); unconfirmed, dropped

limits: No assigned live Wayland lock/display, IME or slow-DPMS hardware. review.py run 20260930T202722Z-a8078f4d covers source-regex positive/mutant and QML text-format scan, not real input event injection. Qt source was read from qt/qtdeclarative 6.10; install/omarchy-base.packages lists quickshell and qt6 modules without exact Qt version; Hyprland producer examined at v0.51.1, package list likewise has no pinned version.

flags.claim: only input that reaches the lock clears it
flags.why: The claim says only input clears the flag, but an output change clears it too: Quickshell's onScreensChanged sets root.displaysBlank = false directly (Service.qml:533-546, line 539 at d64d6f25). Other runWake() callers (submit, failure, unlock; Service.qml:169,218,244,298) all follow input or unlock. My report's F1 kept this qualifier; the draft dropped it. It does not change the finding, because a locked media or brightness key changes no outputs.
flags.fix: only input that reaches the lock, or an output change, clears it
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: 'only input reaching the lock or an output change clears it'

flags.claim: Suggested change: ... polling hyprctl monitors -j while blanked for every wallpaper, not only video.
flags.why: The suggestion reads as a complete fix, but two parts of my suggestion were dropped. (1) The existing monitorDpmsTimer has triggeredOnStart: true (Service.qml:470). If it simply starts when the lock blanks, its first answer can come back before blankProcess has turned the panel off (Service.qml:450-453). That answer says the panel is on, and the real wake key would then be typed for up to 3 s. (2) A poll leaves up to one 3 s interval of exposure (interval: 3000, Service.qml:468). Source reasoning only; not run.
flags.fix: append: '(start the poll after the blank has landed; up to one 3 s poll interval remains)'
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: suggested change now says start the poll after the blank lands and up to one 3 s interval remains

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** On a lit lock screen, the first password key can be dropped because `displaysBlank` can stay true after the panel relights.

### A stale `displaysBlank` drops the first key on a lit screen

`displaysBlank` records what the lock requested (`Service.qml:35-38`); only input reaching the lock or an output change clears it, and with a still wallpaper nothing polls the panel. With Omarchy defaults (`key_press_enables_dpms = true`, media/brightness binds with `locked = true`), such a key lights the panel but Hyprland consumes it. **Impact:** typing `hunter2` + Enter submits `unter2`, a failed attempt that counts toward `pam_faillock`; before this PR it unlocked.

**Suggested change:** Base the swallow on reported DPMS state, e.g. poll `hyprctl monitors -j` while blanked for every wallpaper, starting after the blank lands (up to one 3 s interval remains).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at d64d6f25)</summary>

# Reproducer: a password typed while `displaysBlank` is still set loses its first character

What it shows: `LockView.qml` at the PR head discards the first key whenever `displaysBlank` is true, whether or not the panel is actually dark. The script loads the real `shell/plugins/lock/LockView.qml` in Qt's QML test runner (offscreen, with small stand-ins for `qs.Commons` and `qs.Ui`), wires it the way `Service.qml` does (edits become `passwordText`; `wakeRequested` sets `displaysBlank` to false, as `runWake()` does), and types into it.

Precondition modelled, not run live: the second test starts with `displaysBlank` true on a lit screen. That is the state `Service.qml` is left in after a Hyprland bind marked `locked = true` (brightness, volume, media keys) lights the panel: Hyprland consumes the key for the bind and enables DPMS (`key_press_enables_dpms = true`), so the lock never sees a key and nothing calls `runWake()`. That part comes from source reading (Hyprland 0.56.2 `InputManager.cpp` and `KeybindManager.cpp`, Omarchy `default/hypr/input.lua` and `default/hypr/bindings/media.lua`), not from a live session.

Requires qt6-declarative (for `qmltestrunner` and the `QtTest` QML module). Run from the checkout under test:

```bash
bash repro-lock-wake-key.sh
```

## Script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Drives real key events into shell/plugins/lock/LockView.qml with qmltestrunner
# (Qt's QML test runner, part of qt6-declarative), offscreen, with minimal
# stand-ins for qs.Commons and qs.Ui. Run from an Omarchy checkout:
#   bash repro-lock-wake-key.sh [checkout]
set -euo pipefail

root=${1:-.}
runner=${QMLTESTRUNNER:-/usr/lib/qt6/bin/qmltestrunner}
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$work/imports/qs/Commons" "$work/imports/qs/Ui"
cp "$root/shell/plugins/lock/LockView.qml" "$work/LockView.qml"

cat >"$work/imports/qs/Commons/qmldir" <<'EOF'
module qs.Commons
singleton Border 1.0 Border.qml
singleton Color 1.0 Color.qml
singleton Style 1.0 Style.qml
singleton Util 1.0 Util.qml
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Commons/Style.qml" <<'EOF'
pragma Singleton
import QtQuick
QtObject {
  property QtObject font: QtObject { property int heading: 20; property string family: "sans-serif" }
  property int cornerRadius: 0
}
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Commons/Color.qml" <<'EOF'
pragma Singleton
import QtQuick
QtObject {
  property color background: "black"
  property QtObject lock: QtObject {
    property color background: "#202020"; property color borderError: "red"; property color borderActive: "white"
    property color text: "white"; property color textError: "red"; property color selection: "gray"; property color placeholder: "gray"
  }
}
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Commons/Border.qml" <<'EOF'
pragma Singleton
import QtQuick
QtObject { function surfaceSpec(scope, key, fallback, thickness, alphaKey) { return ({}) } }
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Commons/Util.qml" <<'EOF'
pragma Singleton
import QtQuick
QtObject { function isVideoPath(path) { return false } }
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Ui/qmldir" <<'EOF'
module qs.Ui
BorderSurface 1.0 BorderSurface.qml
BackgroundMedia 1.0 BackgroundMedia.qml
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Ui/BorderSurface.qml" <<'EOF'
import QtQuick
Rectangle { property var borderSpec; property int borderTop: 3; property int borderRight: 3; property int borderBottom: 3; property int borderLeft: 3 }
EOF
cat >"$work/imports/qs/Ui/BackgroundMedia.qml" <<'EOF'
import QtQuick
Item {
  property string path; property int version; property bool playbackEnabled; property bool video: false; property bool ready: false
  property bool cached; property bool constrainDecode; property size decodeSize
}
EOF

cat >"$work/tst_lock_wake_key.qml" <<'EOF'
import QtQuick
import QtTest

Item {
  id: top
  width: 800
  height: 600

  property var submitted: []

  // Wired the way Service.qml wires the real lock: an edit becomes the next
  // passwordText, and wakeRequested runs runWake(), which sets displaysBlank
  // to false.
  function makeView(blank) {
    var c = Qt.createComponent(Qt.resolvedUrl("LockView.qml"), Component.PreferSynchronous)
    var v = c.createObject(top, { width: 800, height: 600, loadBackground: false, displaysBlank: blank })
    v.passwordTextEdited.connect(function(p) { v.passwordText = p })
    v.submitPassword.connect(function(p) { top.submitted.push(p) })
    v.wakeRequested.connect(function() { v.displaysBlank = false })
    v.forcePasswordFocus()
    return v
  }

  TestCase {
    name: "LockWakeKey"
    when: windowShown

    function type(s) { for (var i = 0; i < s.length; i++) keyClick(s[i]) }

    // What the PR sets out to do: the key that wakes a blanked lock is not typed.
    function test_space_that_wakes_a_blanked_lock_is_not_typed() {
      var v = makeView(true)
      wait(0)
      keyClick(Qt.Key_Space)
      compare(JSON.stringify(v.passwordText), JSON.stringify(""), "password after the wake key")
      v.destroy()
    }

    // Pressing a Hyprland bind marked `locked = true` (brightness, volume or
    // media keys) lights the panel through key_press_enables_dpms, but the key
    // never reaches the lock. Nothing calls runWake(), so displaysBlank is
    // still true when the user starts typing on the lit screen.
    function test_password_typed_on_lit_screen_with_stale_blank_flag() {
      top.submitted = []
      var v = makeView(true)
      wait(0)
      type("hunter2")
      keyClick(Qt.Key_Return)
      compare(top.submitted.length, 1, "one submission")
      compare(JSON.stringify(top.submitted[0]), JSON.stringify("hunter2"), "the submitted password")
      v.destroy()
    }
  }
}
EOF

QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software QML_DISABLE_DISK_CACHE=1 \
  "$runner" -import "$work/imports" -input "$work/tst_lock_wake_key.qml"
```

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### The new test checks source text and passes with the swallow broken

Adding `event.accepted = false` after `event.accepted = clearPassword` sends every key back to `TextInput`, yet `lock-wake-key-test.sh` still passes; its `root.wakeRequested()` assertion already holds at the merge base. **Impact:** the test does not protect the behaviour it describes.

**Suggested change:** Move the decision into a small pure JS function (for example `wakeKeyAction(displaysBlank, key, modifiers)`) and test it with `run_node_test`, as `docs/testing.md` describes for shell JavaScript.

# Reproducer: the new test passes when the wake key is typed again

What it shows: `test/shell.d/lock-wake-key-test.sh` matches source text. Adding one line after `event.accepted = clearPassword` makes every key fall through to `TextInput` again, and the test still passes. The behavioural check from the other reproducer (`repro-lock-wake-key.sh`) catches it.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (qmltestrunner, offscreen, real `LockView.qml` with stubbed `qs.Commons`/`qs.Ui`):
- While `displaysBlank` is true, the waking key (Space, a letter, Shift, Enter) is not typed and a buffered password is cleared.
- While awake, typing, Backspace, Enter, Escape and Ctrl+U behave as on the merge base.
- The PR merges cleanly into current `quattro` and behaves the same there.

**Notes:**
- `Keys.priority: Keys.BeforeItem` is Qt's default (`qquickitem.cpp`, `QQuickKeysAttached` constructor), so that line changes nothing; the handler already ran before `TextInput`.
- From source and the harness (auto-repeat not driven directly), only the first key is swallowed; repeats of a held wake key would be typed once the flag clears.
- Clearing on wake also drops a half-typed password after a pause longer than the 5 s idle blank, and Enter pressed while blank does not submit. Commit 71aa17a describes this as intended.

**Related open PRs:** #9211 adds the same wake-key swallow (without the clear) in the same `Keys.onPressed` block, plus a resume wake in `Service.qml` and its own source-text test; it conflicts textually with this PR. #7806, #12667, #13183, #13590 and #12461 also edit that block and conflict textually. #11991 removes the pointer-motion wake; with `mouse_move_enables_dpms = true`, moving the mouse would then also reach the stale-flag case.
</details>
